keyFindings.text: **`serde_json` is configured for bit-exact float parity.** `serde_json = { version = "1", features = ["float_roundtrip", "preserve_order", "unbounded_depth"] }` with the inline comment "float_roundtrip: recorded floats must survive parsing bit for bit." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/Cargo.toml:28-29] The sk-code set warns that `serde_json` does not match JavaScript number spelling [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/quality-standards/determinism-and-parity.md:65] but never names the `float_roundtrip` feature, `preserve_order` or `unbounded_depth`. **LACKS** the feature-flag remedy for the hazard it already names.

**A single crate with a lib+bin split, not a workspace.** `src/lib.rs` declares 69 `pub mod` items plus two private modules (`mime`, and `js_number` behind `#[cfg(test)]`) [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/src/lib.rs:10-78], and `src/main.rs` is a thin front end that imports `rust_anything::{analyze, app, app_shadow, bridge, drift, front_door, gate, harness, lift, mcp, report, shadow}` [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/src/main.rs:21-23]. The sk-code set's only layout is a five-crate workspace whose binary lives in a separate `sidecar` crate [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/quality-standards/build-and-organization.md:235-262]. **LACKS** a single-crate lib+bin layout, which is what a CLI app actually is.

**Edition 2024 and `rust-version = "1.97"`, with the MSRV read back as a compile-time constant.** `pub(crate) const MIN_RUST: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_RUST_VERSION");` makes the declared MSRV the single source of truth instead of a duplicated string. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/Cargo.toml:4] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/Cargo.toml:8] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/src/lib.rs:8] The sk-code set requires edition 2024 and a declared `rust-version` with a 1.85 example [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/quality-standards/build-and-organization.md:40-46], so the declaration is **COVERED**; the `env!("CARGO_PKG_RUST_VERSION")` single-source pattern is **LACKED**.

**Error handling is `anyhow` at every layer, not only at `main`.** `anyhow = "1"` is a direct dependency [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/Cargo.toml:15]; 54 of the 74 files in `src/` import it, and `src/*.rs` carries 462 `bail!` / `.context(` / `with_context(` call sites. `thiserror` is not a dependency at all — it appears only as a string in the crate-recommendation table [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/src/crates.rs:227]. The sk-code set makes this a **P0 violation**: "Do not use `anyhow` in pure-core public APIs or exported functions" [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/quality-standards/docs-errors-and-async.md:147], and the P1 checklist requires "Core errors use typed `thiserror` enums" [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/rust-checklist/p1-required.md:109]. **CONTRADICTS** for an app-shaped crate: the sk-code rule is written for a binding whose core is consumed by adapters, and applied literally it flags rust-anything's own `src/` as a P0 failure.

**rust-anything pins its lint policy inside the single crate's own manifest, not a workspace.** `[lints.rust] unsafe_code = "forbid"` and `[lints.clippy] all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }` sit in the package manifest itself. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/Cargo.toml:42-46] The sk-code set shows only the workspace form `[workspace.lints.rust]` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/quick-reference/rustdoc-and-cargo.md:119] and never shows a single-crate `[lints.*]` block. **LACKS** for an app-style crate.

**serde struct conventions are explicit and uniform.** Report enums carry `#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]` [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/src/analyze.rs:25] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/src/analyze.rs:49]; optional and empty fields carry `skip_serializing_if` [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/src/analyze.rs:123] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/src/analyze.rs:126]; input fields carry `#[serde(default)]` for forward compatibility [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/src/app.rs:89-116]; and the config struct carries `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/src/app.rs:152]. The sk-code set has zero hits for `deny_unknown_fields`, `skip_serializing_if` or `rename_all`. **LACKS** the whole serde-attribute convention.

**Test layout is 46 top-level integration files, one shared helper module, and 30 fixture directories.** `tests/` holds 46 entries including `common/mod.rs` and `fixtures/` [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/tests/common/mod.rs:1], and `tests/fixtures/` holds 30 language-named fixture trees. The sk-code set covers `tests/*.rs` and `tests/common/mod.rs` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/quality-standards/build-and-organization.md:163-164] — **COVERED** — but has zero hits for `tests/fixtures`, so the fixture-tree convention is **LACKED**.

**The clap CLI is derive-first with doc comments as help text.** `#[derive(Parser)]` plus `#[command(name, version, about, after_help)]` [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/src/main.rs:25-31]; a `#[derive(Subcommand)]` enum whose variant doc comments become the subcommand help [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/src/main.rs:52-54]; `ValueEnum` for closed sets [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/src/main.rs:37-50]; and `#[arg(default_value = ".")]` on the root positional [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/src/main.rs:57-58]. The sk-code set has zero hits for `clap`. **LACKS** CLI argument design entirely.

**The finish gate is four commands, and one of them is a doc update.** `CLAUDE.md` says: "Before finishing a change: `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, and update `docs/STATUS.md` when what works changed." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/CLAUDE.md:6-7] The sk-code set carries the clippy form with `--workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/quality-standards/build-and-organization.md:78] — **COVERED** — but has no rule that a change which alters observable behaviour must update a status document. **LACKS** the documentation half of the gate.

**"Keep the original's shape" is an explicit port rule.** "A port keeps the original's units, names and public API: one crate per unit, the same exported functions and classes, the same arguments and errors. The front door keeps the original's commands and flags. … Change the design after the port matches, not during it." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/how-it-works.md:310-316] The sk-code naming reference never mentions the original at all. **LACKS** the shape-preservation rule.

**`bench` is deliberately outside `gate`, because speed decides shipping but is not correctness.** The decision reads: "`bench` is a separate step, not part of `gate`. Speed is not correctness, but it decides whether a port should ship: every x18n core port was correct and slower." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/DECISIONS.md:60] The sk-code set mentions benchmarks only as build hygiene — "Run `cargo test --benches` on pull requests to verify benchmark compilation" [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/quality-standards/build-and-organization.md:218] — and as a precondition for Rayon [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/quality-standards/docs-errors-and-async.md:287]. **LACKS** the rule that a port must be timed against the original before it ships.

**`diff` reports where the first difference is, not just that one exists.** Each mismatch carries `return`, `throw` or `call N`, the JSON path such as `$.items[2].name`, the kind of difference, and for text the character with context; distinct differences are grouped under a short stable id "so 40 failing cases from one bug read as one line", and `--redact` prints shapes only. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/how-it-works.md:40] The sk-code set has no mismatch-reporting rule. **LACKS**.

**`gate` is a composite pass/fail, and two of its clauses have no sk-code equivalent.** The gate covers fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, an `unsafe` audit, nothing unported, a recorded failing case for every error path of the original, no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` where the original returns an error unless marked `// INFALLIBLE: <why>`, build, API, behavior, recording freshness, size ("no more than 3x the original's lines plus 50"), and the cheat guard. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/how-it-works.md:42] The sk-code set covers fmt, clippy and tests [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/quality-standards/build-and-organization.md:78] and denies `unwrap_used`/`expect_used`/`panic` through clippy [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/rust-checklist/p1-required.md:171] — **COVERED** — but has zero hits for `INFALLIBLE`, so the marked escape and the "where the original returns an error" scoping are **LACKED**, as is the 3x-plus-50 size budget.

**`record` generates deterministic edge-case inputs from parameter types plus per-parameter semantic traps, and can also record the original's own test suite.** The traps named are "string length and case, signed division, overflow edges, float printing, map and sort order", saved to `cases.jsonl`, with `--from-tests -- npx jest` to capture every call the original's suite makes and `--float-tolerance` for numeric code. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/how-it-works.md:38] The sk-code set requires golden fixtures and forbids auto-accepting changed goldens [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/quality-standards/determinism-and-parity.md:236] but never says what inputs the recording must contain. **LACKS** the input-generation rule.

**`shadow` runs both implementations in production, returns the original's result, and never lets a Rust error reach a caller.** `RUST_ANYTHING_MODE=old|shadow|new` selects the mode, and the decision records the reason: "Shipping shadow code must not change behavior; only the report sees Rust." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/how-it-works.md:44] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/DECISIONS.md:44] The sk-code set has zero hits for `shadow`. **LACKS** the staged-rollout method entirely.

**A pitfall records that a broken port passed because its case was never recorded, and the remedy is to prove the test can fail.** Recording silently drops a case whose result JSON cannot hold; the only input exercising `'` also decoded ` `, so a port that wrongly decoded `'` passed. The remedy: "After writing inputs for a behavior, check that `cases.jsonl` holds them, and break the port once to see `diff` fail." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/pitfalls.md:112-117] The sk-code set has no "prove the check can fail" rule. **LACKS**.

**A pitfall records that a CLI's recorded writes were invisible because the fixture already held them.** "A CLI that regenerates project files was recorded on a project it had just generated, so every case rewrote files with the bytes they already had, and a front door that wrote nothing passed. Record such CLIs from a fixture whose generated files are stale (overwrite them with a marker first), and check that the `*.out` folders are not empty." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/pitfalls.md:88-93] The sk-code set has no fixture-staleness rule. **LACKS** — and this is the one finding that speaks directly to a CLI-shaped app, which is what the topic asks about.

**A stale recording fails the gate, so an upstream change cannot pass silently.** `record` saves a fingerprint of the unit's files in `recorded-from.json`; when the original changes, `diff` reports a stale recording and exits non-zero, and `gate` fails until the unit is recorded again. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/how-it-works.md:318-322] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/how-it-works.md:262-264] The sk-code set has zero hits for `stale` or `fingerprint`. **LACKS** recording freshness.

**Corrections the user makes during a port are committed as port rules and injected into every later prompt.** They live in `rust/RULES.md`, one bullet each, added with `rules --add`, and "`go` puts them in `TASK.md`, and the MCP server's prompts and instructions carry them, so every later unit and every agent keeps them." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/how-it-works.md:244-248] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/DECISIONS.md:49] The sk-code set has zero hits for `RULES.md`. **LACKS** the durable-correction mechanism.

**The cheat guard is the most transferable rule in the repository: three named checks that stop a port passing without porting.** `literals` fails a port whose own files carry three or more string literals of 8+ characters or numbers of 5+ significant digits that equal a recorded argument or result while the original never spells them out, with `// recorded-literal: <reason>` as the escape; `tests` fails when `#[test]` functions, assertions or `#[ignore]`s drop below the last passing gate; `recording` fails when a recorded line was edited or removed. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/how-it-works.md:225-241] The reason is stated as a decision: "Agents told to make every case pass sometimes hard-code results, delete failing tests or edit the recording; `diff` alone cannot tell." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/DECISIONS.md:49] The sk-code set has zero hits for `cheat`, `recorded-literal` or `known-diffs`. **LACKS** — and this is the gap with the highest value for an agent-driven port.

**The method is a nine-stage pipeline with the original as the source of truth.** `profile → analyze → bridge → record → port.rs → diff → bench → shadow → gate`, and the doc states the invariant plainly: "The original stays the source of truth: `record` runs it on edge cases (and your own inputs) and saves what it returns or throws; `diff` replays every case against the Rust; nothing ships until they all match and `gate` passes." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/how-it-works.md:7-14] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/how-it-works.md:16-18] The sk-code set states the parity *standard* — "Rust output must be byte-for-byte identical to the pinned TypeScript oracle" [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/quality-standards/determinism-and-parity.md:38] — but has no ordered stage sequence that produces the evidence. **LACKS** the pipeline.

**"refused" is a first-class outcome, not a failure.** "`refused` means the function stays in its language. The note is the reason `bridge` prints, where it names the type." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/types.md:13] TypeScript refuses `(x: number) => number`/`Function`, `RegExp` and `Iterator`/`Generator` [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/types.md:44-46]; Python refuses `Callable`, `Iterator`, `Generator`, `*args`, `**kwargs` and decorators other than `@cache` and `@lru_cache` [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/types.md:88-90]. The sk-code set has zero hits for `refused`. **LACKS** the "keep it in the original language" verdict, which is the decision that stops a port from silently changing a public API.

**`docs/types.md` has no PyO3 section, so the topic's premise overstates the source.** The Python section maps Python source types to Rust port types and never names PyO3 [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/types.md:64-91]; PyO3 appears only as the Python bridge in the website docs — "Python | PyO3 (abi3), direct conversion, typed exceptions" [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/website/pages/en/docs/concepts/bridge.md:27]. The sk-code set also has zero hits for `PyO3`. **CONTRADICTS** the topic's framing: there is no PyO3 value-class mapping to import, only a bridge name. The honest edit is to add a PyO3 bridge row to sk-code's interop model, not a value table.

**`docs/types.md` is a per-language source-type → port-type table, and the contract is stated up front.** "`bridge` reads each exported function's types from the source and writes the port's signature in `port.rs` from them. This page lists, per language, what a source type becomes there, and which types keep a function in its language, with the reason `bridge` gives." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/types.md:3-5] The sk-code Rust set has no source-type → Rust-type mapping table at all. **LACKS**.

**`serde_json::Value` is the explicit escape hatch for anything the mapping does not know.** "`serde_json::Value` means the value crosses as JSON as it is: objects, maps, unions of different types and anything the mapping does not know." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/types.md:12] The sk-code set has zero hits for `serde_json::Value`. **LACKS** the named fallback type.

**A defaulted parameter becomes `Option<T>`, with one per-language exception.** "A parameter with a default becomes `Option<T>`, unless the default is a literal Rust can write (a number, `true`/`false` or a plain string), in Python, Ruby, PHP and C#. In TypeScript and JavaScript every parameter with a default is `Option<T>`." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/types.md:14] The sk-code set has no default-parameter rule. **LACKS**.

**C pointers are mapped by their neighbouring parameter, and every other pointer is refused with a named design question.** `const char *` → `Option<&[u8]>`; a const byte pointer followed by an integer length → `&[u8]` with the length left out of the port; a writable byte pointer with a size → `&mut [u8]`; a pointer to a scalar the function writes → `Option<&mut T>`; `char **` pointing into a string parameter → `Option<&mut Option<usize>>`; a by-value all-scalar struct → a `#[repr(C)]` struct. "Any other pointer, array or function pointer parameter is refused ('ownership must be designed'), and so are any other returned pointer ('who frees it must be designed') and variadic functions." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/types.md:154-168] The sk-code set has zero hits for `repr(C)`. **LACKS** — and the refusal wording is the valuable part, because it turns pointer ownership into a design decision instead of a guess.

**The C ABI keeps width and sign through `std::ffi`.** `int` → `std::ffi::c_int`, `long` → `std::ffi::c_long` with the note "32 bits on Windows", `size_t`/`uintptr_t` → `usize`, `ssize_t`/`ptrdiff_t`/`intptr_t` → `isize`, `float` → `f32`, `double` → `f64`, `bool`/`_Bool` → `bool`, and `long double`/`wchar_t` refused as "not a C scalar the bridge knows". Specifiers may come in any order, `const` and `volatile` are ignored, an `enum` is `std::ffi::c_int`, and a project `typedef` of a scalar is that scalar. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/types.md:123-152] The sk-code set has zero hits for `std::ffi`, `c_int` or `c_char`. **LACKS** the C ABI entirely.

**The integer mapping is per source language, not global.** TypeScript `number` → `f64` [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/types.md:28] while Python `int` → `i64` [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/types.md:68]. The sk-code set mentions `f64` in 18 files and `i64` in 3, but never frames the choice as a per-source-language decision. **PARTIAL** — the JavaScript case is covered implicitly by the TypeScript-oracle framing; the Python case is absent.

**The mapping table is executable, so it cannot drift from the code.** "`cargo test --test types_doc` checks every row against the mapping, so a row that no longer matches the code fails the build." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/types.md:16] The test does it by `include_str!("../docs/types.md")` and iterating the documented rows against `bridge::param_type` and the per-language modules [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/tests/types_doc.rs:1-5] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/tests/types_doc.rs:16]. The sk-code set has no rule that a documented mapping table must be tested against the implementation. **LACKS** — and this is the most portable single rule in the file, because it applies to any standards document that carries a table.

**The port error contract is uniform and untyped: `Result<T, String>`.** "A port function returns `Result<T, String>` and the table gives the `T`; in C it returns `T`, as the C function does." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/docs/types.md:10] The sk-code set requires typed `thiserror` enums in the core [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/rust-checklist/p1-required.md:109] and forbids `anyhow` in pure-core public APIs [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/quality-standards/docs-errors-and-async.md:147]. **CONTRADICTS** on the surface, but the scopes differ: rust-anything's `port.rs` is a generated scaffold whose error text is deliberately not compared (see iteration 2, finding on `L7`), while sk-code's rule governs a shipped public API. Recorded as a scope conflict, not a sk-code error.

**`whole-app.md` is a session-spanning protocol built on a claimable map.** "A whole-app port outlasts one session, so `rust/MAP.md` carries it between sessions: the goal, an index of the ADRs in `DECISIONS.md`, every unit of the plan with its state (`open`, `claimed by <session> <date>`, `done`), open questions, and what is out of scope. … A session **claims** one unit in the map before it starts, ports that unit, and marks it `done` with its gate and replay results. A claimed unit belongs to its session: pick another. A new session starts by reading `MAP.md`, then `HANDOFF.md` when there is one." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/skills/rust-anything/whole-app.md:17-25] The sk-code set has no multi-session protocol. **LACKS**.

**`whole-app.md` opens with a structured interview whose shape is a design tree asked in rounds.** "Interview the user until every decision the port depends on is settled. Map them as a **design tree**: each decision branches into the ones that hang off it. Ask in **rounds**: a round is the whole **frontier**, every decision whose prerequisites are already settled. Number each question, give your recommended answer, and word it so \"yes\" accepts the recommendation." [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/skills/rust-anything/whole-app.md:37-46] The seed branches are shape, scope, equivalence bar, compatibility, dependencies, targets, checkpoints and cutover [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.Trash/rust-anything-main/skills/rust-anything/whole-app.md:58-66]. The sk-code set has no interview protocol. **LACKS**.

**Port rules are read before writing and appended the moment the user corrects behaviour.** "Before writing code, run `rust-anything rules <repo>` and follow every rule it lists: behavior the user already corrected in an earlier unit. Each time the user corrects how the port behaves, add it right away with `rust-anything rules <repo> --add \"<the rule, in one sentence>\"`, so the next unit and the next agent keep it."
